plain_language: Direction of the cost change. Positive means the attacked OPF is more expensive than the matching normal OPF; negative means it is cheaper.
Size of the cost change caused by the attack, ignoring whether the cost went up or down.
Cost change scaled by the normal cost for the same load profile, so systems and seasons are easier to compare.
Total fleet redispatch over the 24-hour day. This is the main proof that a one-generator attack can move the wider system.
How much the attacked generator itself moved across the day.
How much all other generators moved to compensate. This is the clean system-wide consequence metric.
Total change in network flows over all modeled directed line-flow variables and hours.
Total change in hour-to-hour generator movement across the fleet. It separates a simple output shift from an attack that changes operating movement over the day.
